validated_results.title: Zinc intake from supplements and diet and prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study reporting risk of incident prostate cancer associated with zinc intake.

extraction.population: Men aged 50-76 years in western Washington State enrolled in the VITAL cohort

sample_size.excerpt: Association of sociodemographic, medical, and lifestyle characteristics with prostate cancer among 35,244 men in the VITAL cohort

cases.excerpt: A total of 832 incidents, invasive prostate cancers were diagnosed between baseline (2000-2002) and December 31, 2004.
cases.location: Methods, Follow-up of Subjects for Prostate Cancer and Censoring, paragraph 1

effect_size.excerpt: Ten-year average intake of supplemental zinc was not associated with a reduced prostate cancer risk overall (adjusted hazard ratio (HR) = 0.82 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.58-1.14) for >15mg/day versus non-use, p for trend = 0.44); however, risk of advanced prostate cancer (regionally invasive or distant metastatic, n =123) decreased with greater intake of supplemental zinc (adjusted HR = 0.34 (95% CI 0.13-1.09) for 10-year average intake >15mg/day vs.

confidence_interval.excerpt: After adjustment for confounders, we observed a weak, non-significant inverse association between 10-yr average supplemental zinc and prostate cancer risk (HR = 0.82 (95% CI 0.58 – 1.14) for greater than 15 mg/day versus no use, p for trend = 0.44) ( Table 2 ).

design.excerpt: We evaluated the association between dietary and supplemental zinc and prostate cancer within the VITamins And Lifestyle (VITAL) cohort

timing.excerpt: We have prospectively collected detailed measures of zinc intake from diet and supplements, as well as other factors such as demographic and lifestyle characteristics, in a large cohort study.

continent.excerpt: living in a 13-county area of western Washington State.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: The questionnaire assessed the use of 38 vitamins, mineral, herbal, and other supplements over the 10 years prior to enrollment into the study.
